title: Fail a release only on real differences in a replayed response

blocks.text: Before each release the team replays a day of recorded requests through the new build, against a host simulator like the ones in unit c16, and compares every response the new build gets with the response recorded for the same request. Some fields differ on every run by design: the transmission time, the STAN, the retrieval reference number. The release fails when anything else differs.
The check has started failing releases that changed nothing, and nobody reads its report any more. Finish the three methods marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ReplayCheck.java`:

items: `same`: whether two values of a field are equal;

blocks.text: `differences` returns the paths on which the two responses differ (`"39"`, `"48.2"`), in field order, leaving out the paths it was told change every run. When you're done, a replay that matches its recording returns an empty list, and a replay that doesn't names exactly the paths that changed. About ten lines in total.
The tests compare responses built in code and responses unpacked from the bytes the simulator sent, with chip data and with sub-fields.

cases.says: a replayed response that differs only in the fields that change every run has no differences, built or unpacked
a changed, a missing and an added field are each reported once by number
binary values are equal when their bytes are equal, even in two different arrays
sub-fields are compared one by one and reported by their dotted path, a sub-field that changes every run is left out, and a nested field missing on one side is reported sub-field by sub-field
the bitmap an unpacked response keeps is not a difference, so a missing field is reported once
differences come in ascending field order, including fields only the replayed response carries

origin.section: 17.3 Two Messages Are Compared Field by Field, and Binary Fields by Content

concepts: Two messages are compared field by field in field order, without the bitmap, binary values by content and nested fields sub-field by sub-field.
